candidate.title: Coquitlam protects Partington Creek wildlife corridor
candidate.commercialFitReason: No commercial fit is asserted. Editorial utility, locality, source support, and brand safety qualified the candidate first.
candidate.lengthRationale: Bulletin treatment is appropriate because the official source supplies a concise civic update with clear location, proposal stage, habitat details, and resident impact.

evidence.readerImpact: Residents can understand where the proposed Burke Mountain habitat corridor would be protected, how wide it would be, and how it connects to development approvals.
evidence.freshnessEvidence: City of Coquitlam page is posted July 27, 2026, with a July 20, 2026 city release date.
evidence.uniqueAngleEvidence: No current published Trends Today article covers the Partington Creek wildlife corridor or the Burke Mountain development-approval protection mechanism.
claimSupport: City says the corridor would connect Pinecone Burke Provincial Park, Minnekhada Regional Park, and surrounding Burke Mountain green spaces.
City says monitoring captured more than 400,000 wildlife images documenting 57 species.
City says the first phase would run between Cedar Drive and Victoria Drive, include a 50-metre corridor, and widen to 100 metres at a wildlife hot spot.
City says the first development proposal received first reading May 25, 2026 and second and third readings after a June 22, 2026 public hearing.
